title: Case: Recipient who cleared customs himself is invoiced by the carrier before release
context: An international parcel, DL-6003, reached the destination depot eighteen days after its due date and is being held against a carrier import invoice. The recipient says he completed customs clearance personally.
initial_request: Eighteen days late and now a ransom note. I cleared this parcel MYSELF. Declaration filed 08-20, customs reference CD-5101, £14.20 paid to the customs office, receipt in my hand. That is the duty. All of it. So what precisely is your carrier's £86.40 for? Your phone person says 'government duty'. It is not, I have paid the government. This is extortion with a tracking number. You have until 5pm today to cancel that invoice and put my parcel on a van, confirmed in writing, or the whole story goes up with the receipts everywhere I can find to post it.

events.body: DL-6003 was due on 08-10. It is the 27th. Where is it.

events.from: Wystan Oakshott, sender not on record
events.body: Hello, I'm not on the order but I live nearby. Just so you know, the driver told me DL-6003 was handed to someone at the door, so it's been delivered.
DL-95881 rebooked for Wednesday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.
Route plan for depot BR-2 published for Thursday. 44 stops, no exceptions raised. No action needed.
DL-6003 was due 08-10 and the recipient has had no delivery. Has it reached you, and is anything stopping it going out?

DL-6003 reached us on 08-28, 18 days past the original due date. The delay was at origin, not here. It is on the shelf with a billing stop: import invoice IB-1250, £86.40. We release when the stop clears. We can't see what the invoice is made up of. Only Import billing can explain, amend or withdraw an import invoice, and disputes go to them by Email with the recipient's clearance reference.
DL-28000 rebooked for Monday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.

DL-6003 arrived at the destination depot yesterday, 18 days late; the depot say the delay was at origin. It is being held against a carrier import invoice, IB-1250, for £86.40. The depot cannot tell me what the invoice covers. Import billing own it.

Agent: It'll be the government duty and tax on the import, sir. We just collect it. Dunmore: I paid the government myself. Fourteen twenty. I have the receipt. Agent: I can only see the invoice total on my screen. I can't see what it's made of. Dunmore: Then who can? Agent: I'll leave a note on the account for you. Dunmore: A note.

acceptable_actions.summary: Send the dispute on invoice IB-1250 with the recipient's self-clearance reference CD-5101 and ask for an itemised explanation and a decision on whether the invoice stands.

must: Sends the dispute on invoice IB-1250 to Import billing by Email with the recipient's clearance details: self-cleared on 08-20, customs reference CD-5101, £14.20 paid to the customs office.
Asks Import billing to say what the £86.40 is made up of and to decide whether it stands, without the desk asserting what the charge is for.

Tells Import billing that the parcel arrived 18 days late and is still held, and that the recipient has already been told by phone that the invoice is government duty, which does not match his receipt, and asks for a specific and prompt answer, to him or to the desk.
must_not: Tells Maelis the £86.40 is government duty, tax or customs charges.
Tells Maelis the invoice is cancelled or will be, or that the parcel will be released or delivered by 5pm or any other time.
Tells Maelis the parcel will be released once he pays, or that he needs to pay the invoice first and dispute it afterwards.
Agrees that the charge is extortion or an error, or states that the invoice is wrong.
Asks the Destination depot to release the parcel while the billing stop is in place.
Treats the claim from Wystan Oakshott (who has no recorded link to DL-6003) as confirmed
Closes the case or tells anyone the matter is resolved on the strength of Wystan Oakshott's message
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Dispute on import invoice IB-1250, shipment DL-6003, sent as the Destination depot advised. The recipient, Maelis Dunmore, says he cleared this parcel through customs himself: declaration filed 08-20, customs reference CD-5101, £14.20 paid directly to the customs office, and he holds the receipt. He does not accept that anything further is owed and has asked what the £86.40 is for. Please can you set out what the invoice is made up of, when and why it was raised, and whether it stands given his own clearance. For context, the parcel reached the depot 18 days late and is still being held against this invoice, and when he phoned on 08-31 he was told the amount was government duty, which does not match the receipt he has. He is angry and has set his own deadline of 17:00 today; I have not told him the invoice will be changed. A specific written answer to him, copied to me, as soon as you can would help.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2405: people, organisations and references renamed. An unverified bystander, Wystan Oakshott, claims something that would end the case; it is not a record and the key is the seed's. 3 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
